reviewed_proof_input_text:
# Actual Gibbs diffuseness from edge-local symmetric-pressure optimality

Independent proof draft, 2026-09-05. This is an all-orders finite-temperature
theorem. It does not prove convergence of the original MO sequence.

Let `E` be the unordered edges of `K_N`, let `K=binom(N,2)`, and let
`A_e in {-1,1}`. For positive edge strengths `u_e`, put

\[
H_A(x)=\sum_{e=\{i,j\}}u_e A_e x_ix_j,\qquad
F(A)=\log\mathbb E_x\cosh H_A(x).
\]

Use the actual augmented Gibbs measure on `(sigma,x) in {+1,-1}^{N+1}`
with density proportional to `exp(sigma H_A(x))`, and define

\[
\Gamma_e=\mathbb E[\sigma x_i x_j],\qquad r_e=A_e\Gamma_e.
\]

Assume only that flipping any single sign of `A` cannot lower `F`.
Every global minimizer over complete signings satisfies this assumption.

## 1. Exact local bound and radial positivity

Flipping edge `e` gives exactly

\[
\exp(F(A^{e})-F(A))
=\cosh(2u_e)-r_e\sinh(2u_e)\ge1.
\]

Consequently

\[
r_e\le\tanh u_e.                                             \tag{1}
\]

For every fixed signing, without any optimality assumption, radial
differentiation gives

\[
\sum_e u_e r_e
=\frac{\mathbb E_x[H_A(x)\sinh H_A(x)]}
       {\mathbb E_x\cosh H_A(x)}\ge0.                         \tag{2}
\]

The pointwise inequality `z sinh(z)>=0` proves the last step. Combining
(1)--(2), with `r_+=max(r,0)`, proves

\[
\boxed{\sum_e u_e|\Gamma_e|
=2\sum_e u_e(r_e)_+-\sum_eu_er_e
\le2\sum_eu_e\tanh u_e
\le2\sum_eu_e^2.}                                           \tag{3}
\]

No cavity limit, deformation, entropy approximation, or transfer between
Gibbs measures is used.

## 2. Equal critical strengths and signed replica observables

For `u_e=beta=c/sqrt(N)`, equation (3) gives

\[
\sum_e|\Gamma_e|\le2K\tanh\beta.
\]

Extend the matrix by `Gamma_ii=E sigma`. Since every entry has magnitude
at most one,

\[
\boxed{\|\Gamma\|_F^2
\le N+2\sum_e|\Gamma_e|
\le N+4K\tanh\beta.}                                       \tag{4}
\]

This is `o(N^2)` whenever `beta_N -> 0`; fixed finite `c` is one example.
For independent replicas from this same actual Gibbs measure and every
real diagonal `D` with `||D||op<=1`,

\[
\left|\mathbb E[\sigma\sigma'(x^TDx')^2]\right|
=|\operatorname{tr}(D\Gamma D\Gamma)|
\le\|\Gamma\|_F^2.                                         \tag{5}
\]

This is a signed correlation matrix, not an assertion of positive
semidefiniteness or a bound for the unsigned spin covariance.

## 3. Separate group positivity and the balanced two-block profile

Let `N=2n` and `0<t<=1`. Give the two internal blocks strength
`u_I=c sqrt((2-t)/N)` and the cross rectangle strength
`u_C=c sqrt(t/N)`. There are `n(n-1)` internal edges and `n^2` cross edges.
Write `I=Q_(A_L)(x)+Q_(A_R)(y)` and `C=x^T B y`. Pairing `y` with `-y`
gives the exact identity, for every signing and `u,v>=0`,

\[
Z(u,v)=\mathbb E\cosh(uI+vC)
      =\mathbb E[\cosh(uI)\cosh(vC)].
\]

Both partial derivatives are nonnegative: their numerators are respectively
`E[I sinh(uI) cosh(vC)]` and `E[C sinh(vC) cosh(uI)]`. Hence the sums of
`r_e` are nonnegative separately on the internal-edge group and the cross
rectangle. This does not assert separate positivity for each diagonal
block on its own. At an edge-local pressure minimum, therefore,

\[
\sum_{e\in g}|\Gamma_e|\le2K_g\tanh u_g\quad(g=I,C).
                                                                    \tag{6}
\]

Using the critical strengths above gives uniformly for `0<=t<=1`,

\[
\sum_e|\Gamma_e|
\le\frac{cN^{3/2}}2\bigl(\sqrt{2-t}+\sqrt t\bigr)
\le cN^{3/2}.                                                \tag{7}
\]

At `t=0`, all cross correlations vanish by the same block-flip symmetry.
The weaker global radial calculation remains consistent:

\[
\sum_eu_e^2=c^2(N/2-1+t/2)\le c^2N/2,
\]

In particular, for `0<t<=1` the squared-correlation term in the
Gaussian-shaped derivative satisfies

\[
\left|\frac12\sum_e(u_e^2)'r_e^2\right|
\le\frac{c^2}{2N}\sum_e|\Gamma_e|
\le\frac{c^3\sqrt N}{4}\bigl(\sqrt{2-t}+\sqrt t\bigr)
\le\frac{c^3\sqrt N}{2}.                                   \tag{8}
\]

Its integral over `0<t<1` is at most `c^3 sqrt(N)/2`. Thus this particular
signed-square contribution is lower order for the actual profile
minimizers with a uniform endpoint bound. No optimizer is asserted to
remain the same as `t` varies.

## 4. The optimized path is absolutely continuous

For the balanced profile define

\[
F_A(t)=\log\mathbb E_x\cosh\bigl(u_I(t)I_A(x)+u_C(t)C_A(x)\bigr),
\qquad f_N(t)=\min_A F_A(t),\qquad 0\le t\le1.
\]

The minimum is over all complete signings of order `N`, not a prescribed
matrix family. Every branch is continuous on the closed interval and
continuously differentiable on the open interval. For every branch,

\[
|F_A'(t)|\le K_I|u_I'(t)|+K_C|u_C'(t)|.                      \tag{9}
\]

The right side is independent of `A` and integrable on `[0,1]`; its only
singularity is `O(t^(-1/2))`. The branches, and then their finite minimum,
are absolutely continuous. For the last assertion use the common bound
`|f_N(b)-f_N(a)|<=integral_a^b [K_I|u_I'|+K_C|u_C'|]`.

Choose the lexicographically first minimizing signing `A(t)`. This is a
Borel measurable selection, since there are finitely many continuous
branches and their comparison sets are Borel. Wherever `f_N` is
differentiable in `(0,1)`, every active branch has derivative `f_N'(t)`:
the differentiable function `F_A-f_N` has a local minimum of zero there.
Consequently the following derivative calculations freeze the active
optimizer and hold almost everywhere, without differentiating `A(t)`.
All correlations and defects below use its actual Gibbs measure.

## 5. Exact scalar-defect reduction of the path

Define, for `u>=0`,

\[
h(u)=\tanh u-u\operatorname{sech}^2u.
\]

One has `h(0)=0` and

\[
h'(u)=2u\operatorname{sech}^2u\tanh u\in[0,2u^2],
\qquad 0\le h(u)\le\frac23u^3.                              \tag{10}
\]

At the selected optimizer put

\[
d_e(t)=u_e(t)(1-r_e(t)^2)+h(u_e(t))-r_e(t)\ge0.               \tag{11}
\]

For fixed `u`, the expression in (11) is concave as a function of
`r in [-1,tanh(u)]`. It equals zero at the right endpoint and
`1+h(u)>0` at the left endpoint, proving the stated nonnegativity by (1).

Define the single weighted defect imbalance

\[
\mathcal D_N(t)=
\sum_{e\in C}\frac{c}{2\sqrt N\sqrt t}\,d_e(t)
-\sum_{e\in I}\frac{c}{2\sqrt N\sqrt{2-t}}\,d_e(t).
                                                                    \tag{12}
\]

It is measurable and integrable: the defects are bounded for fixed `N,c`
and the displayed weights have only the integrable endpoint singularity.
The exact derivative decomposition is

\[
\begin{aligned}
f_N'(t)
&=\sum_eu'_e r_e\\
&=\frac12\sum_e(u_e^2)'(1-r_e^2)
  +\sum_eu'_e h(u_e)-\mathcal D_N(t).
\end{aligned}                                                       \tag{13}
\]

Since `K_C-K_I=n=N/2`, the constant part is exactly

\[
\frac12\sum_e(u_e^2)'=\frac{c^2}{4}.                         \tag{14}
\]

Equation (8) bounds the integral of the signed-square remainder by
`c^3 sqrt(N)/2`. Also, using (10) and
`|(u_e^2)'|=c^2/N`,

\[
\sum_e|u'_e|h(u_e)
\le\frac{c^2}{3N}\sum_eu_e^2
\le\frac{c^4}{6}.                                           \tag{15}
\]

Integrating the almost-everywhere identity (13) therefore proves

\[
\boxed{
f_N(1)-f_N(0)
=\frac{c^2}{4}-\int_0^1\mathcal D_N(t)\,dt+\mathcal E_N(c),
\qquad
|\mathcal E_N(c)|\le\frac{c^3\sqrt N}{2}+\frac{c^4}{6}.
}                                                                  \tag{16}
\]

In particular the looser error `c^3 sqrt(N)+c^4/6` is valid. For every
fixed `c`, the error is `o(N)`. No sign or lower-order bound for the
integral of the defect imbalance has been proved.

## 6. Endpoint scope and remaining implications

Let

\[
P_k(c)=\min_{A\text{ of order }k}
       \log\mathbb E_x\cosh\bigl(cQ_A(x)/\sqrt k\bigr).
\]

The endpoint at one is exactly `f_N(1)=P_N(c)`. The endpoint at zero is

\[
\boxed{
f_N(0)=\min_{A_L,A_R}
 \log\mathbb E_{x,y}\cosh\left(
   \frac c{\sqrt n}[Q_{A_L}(x)+Q_{A_R}(y)]\right),
\qquad N=2n.
}                                                                  \tag{17}
\]

It is NOT automatically `2P_n(c)`. There is only one shared sign in this
symmetric pressure, and the two one-sided pressures can cancel. In fact
`f_N(0)<=2P_n(c)`: choose an order-`n` symmetric-pressure minimizer `A`,
take `A_L=A, A_R=-A`, and write `Z_+=E exp(cQ_A/sqrt(n))`,
`Z_-=E exp(-cQ_A/sqrt(n))`. The endpoint partition function is `Z_+Z_-`,
which is at most `[(Z_++Z_-)/2]^2`.

Thus both the defect integral in (16) and an appropriate comparison of
(17) with `2P_n(c)` still require justification before this path could
give approximate pressure superadditivity. Neither a separate small
defect assumption nor a separate small endpoint-gap assumption is
asserted necessary for every possible proof of the original problem.

The minimizers here are finite-temperature pressure minimizers (or, for
Sections 1--3 alone, single-edge local minima), not automatically exact
minimizers of the zero-temperature norm. No convergence, limiting value,
or sufficient cross-order error estimate is claimed.
